title: Deduplicate events and customer versions, then aggregate revenue by country
objective_text: Deduplicate with dropDuplicates and a latest-row window, then aggregate with count, distinct count, sum and mean.
scenario: Finance's revenue-by-country dashboard disagrees with the ledger. The order feed sometimes delivers an event twice, and the customer table keeps every version of a customer, so customers who moved are counted in both countries. Build gold.revenue_by_country so the numbers match.
engine_label: DuckDB's PySpark API on this PC (not Apache Spark)
starting_environment: Delta tables bronze.order_events and bronze.customer_versions in the exercise folder, and a starter answer.py.
required: Use each customer's latest country (largest valid_from).
Per country: customers (distinct), orders, revenue as decimal(12,2) and avg_order rounded to 2 places.
Write gold.revenue_by_country with country, customers, orders, revenue, avg_order, so that running the code again leaves the same table.

expected.description: Three countries: ES with 2 customers, 3 orders and 65.00; FR with 1, 1 and 15.00; PT with 1, 2 and 60.00.

verifies: Your PySpark deduplicates by event id and by latest version and aggregates per country, on the exercise data and on rows you haven't seen, on this PC.
Running it again leaves the same table.
does_not_verify: It doesn't run on Apache Spark or in a Databricks workspace, and it doesn't check approx_count_distinct, whose estimate can differ between engines.
hints: events.dropDuplicates(["event_id"]) keeps one row per event; deduplicating on customer_id and amount would also drop real orders.
Window.partitionBy("customer_id").orderBy(F.col("valid_from").desc()) with F.row_number() == 1 gives each customer's current country.
Join the events to the current customers on customer_id, then groupBy("country").
F.countDistinct("customer_id") counts customers; F.count("*") counts orders.
explanation: Drop redelivered events by event_id, not by business columns, which would also merge two real orders of the same amount. Keep each customer's latest version with row_number over a window partitioned by customer and ordered by valid_from descending, so a customer who moved counts only in their current country. Then join and aggregate per country with a distinct customer count, a row count, the sum cast to decimal(12,2) and the rounded average, and overwrite the gold table.
troubleshooting: Revenue is too high: redelivered events are counted again; drop duplicates by event_id.
A customer is counted in two countries: every version of the customer was joined; keep the latest.
customers equals orders: count distinct customer ids, not rows.
reset: Reset rebuilds the bronze tables from setup.sql, removes gold.revenue_by_country and puts the starter back.
cleanup: Everything lives in this exercise's folder on this PC; Reset or removing the exercise deletes it. Nothing is created in any workspace.
